name: colDiffs
title: Calculates difference for each column in a matrix

origin.description: Calculates difference for each row (column) in a matrix.
origin.usage:
colDiffs(x, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, lag = 1L, differences = 1L,
  dim. = dim(x), ..., useNames = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An NxK matrix or, if dim. is specified, an N * K vector.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of rows to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of columns to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: differences
arguments.text: An integer specifying the order of difference.

arguments.name: dim.
arguments.text: An integer vector of length two specifying the dimension of x, also when x is not a matrix.

arguments.name: useNames
arguments.text: If TRUE (default), names attributes of the result are set, otherwise not.

origin.details: The difference is taken down the rows within each selected column. It calls the same routine as rowDiffs() with byrow FALSE. The result has N - differences * lag rows, or zero rows when that quantity is negative, and one column per selected column. The installed function returns an integer matrix when x is integer.
origin.value: A matrix with max(0, N - differences * lag) rows and one column per selected column. Integer x returns integer. Double x returns double.

translation.description: Calculates difference for each column in a matrix.
translation.usage:
colDiffs(x, rows=None, cols=None, lag=1, differences=1, dim=None,
  use_names=True)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An N by K array, or a one-dimensional vector when dim is given. A two-dimensional array is read with axis 0 as rows and axis 1 as columns, matching the printed R matrix. Logical x is rejected.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: 1-based rows to include. None uses every row. The difference follows this order down each column.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: 1-based columns to include. None uses every column. Zeros are dropped and negative values exclude, as in R.

arguments.name: lag
arguments.text: Lag, as a positive integer. The default is 1. A non-integer is truncated toward zero, as R's as.integer does.

arguments.name: differences
arguments.text: Order of difference, as a positive integer. The default is 1. A non-integer is truncated toward zero.

arguments.name: dim
arguments.text: Two integers giving the shape of x, also when x is not a matrix. This is dim. When x is one-dimensional, the values fill that shape in column-major order.

arguments.name: use_names
arguments.text: Accepted for compatibility with useNames. The result is always a plain array; names are not attached.

translation.details: The differences come from the rowdiffs crate, ported from matrixStats src/rowDiffs.c with byrow FALSE. The result has max(0, N - differences * lag) rows and one column per selected column. Integer input returns int32. The subtraction wraps, and a wrapped value of -2147483648 is the int32 missing sentinel, with no warning. Double missing values are NaN.
translation.value: An array of shape (max(0, selected rows - differences * lag), selected columns). Double x returns float64. Integer x returns int32.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.rowdiffs import colDiffs

colDiffs(np.arange(1, 13).reshape((4, 3), order="F"))
